issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking specific performance concerning immovable property and possession must be brought in the court within whose territorial jurisdiction the property is situated, unless the relief falls within the limited personal-obedience exception.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of an agreement concerning a residential plot and sought delivery of possession of that plot.
The plot was situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of the court where the suit was filed.
The relief sought included directing the defendant to execute a sale deed and deliver possession.
issues.conclusion: The suit fell within Section 16(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, and its proviso did not apply; the court where the plot was situated was the proper court, so the plaint was correctly ordered returned for presentation to that court.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 16(d) and its proviso of the Code of Civil Procedure require suits concerning rights or interests in immovable property to be instituted where the property is situated. The proviso is limited to cases in which the relief can entirely be obtained through the defendant’s personal obedience and does not enlarge the main provision. Section 20 is residuary and does not displace the limitations in Sections 15 to 19. The Court relied on the principle in Ewing v. Ewing and the treatment of a specific-performance-and-possession suit in New Mofussil Co. Ltd. v. Shankerlal Narayandas Mundade.

rule.if: immovable_property_suit and property_outside_forum and relief_seeks_possession and not relief_entirely_personal_obedience

predicates.immovable_property_suit: The proceeding is a suit concerning rights or interests in immovable property.
predicates.property_outside_forum: The property is situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of the court where the suit was filed.
predicates.relief_seeks_possession: The plaintiff seeks delivery of possession of the property.
predicates.relief_entirely_personal_obedience: The relief sought can be obtained entirely through the defendant’s personal obedience.

issues.definition: When a suit concerning immovable property seeks possession, the property-situs court must hear it if the property is outside the filed court’s territory and the relief is not entirely obtainable through personal obedience.

issues.legal_issue: An agreement selecting a forum cannot confer jurisdiction on a court that otherwise lacks it, although parties may select one court among courts that already have jurisdiction.
material_facts: The agreement stated that courts in the selected city alone would have jurisdiction over disputes arising from the transaction.
The plot was situated outside that city, and the suit sought specific performance concerning the plot and its possession.
The plaintiff relied on the agreement and on the fact that the transaction and payments had connections with the selected city.
issues.conclusion: The forum-selection clause could not give the selected court jurisdiction because that court lacked jurisdiction over the suit; such a clause is effective only when the selected court is one of two or more courts otherwise competent to hear the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure is subject to the limitations in Sections 15 to 19, and a contractual clause cannot confer jurisdiction on a court that lacks it under the Code. Where two or more courts are competent, parties may agree to submit to one of them without contravening Section 28 of the Contract Act, 1872. The Court relied principally on Hakam Singh v. Gamon (India) Ltd. and the cases following it, including Globe Transport Corporation v. Triveni Engineering Works, A.B.C. Laminart (P) Ltd. v. A.P. Agency, Salem, and New Moga Transport Co. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.forum_selection_agreement: The parties agreed that disputes would be heard in a specified court or group of courts.
predicates.selected_forum_lacks_independent_jurisdi: The selected court does not otherwise have jurisdiction to hear the suit.

issues.definition: A forum-selection agreement cannot make a selected court competent when that court otherwise lacks jurisdiction over the civil suit.

issues.legal_issue: A defect in subject-matter jurisdiction cannot be cured by consent, admission, waiver, acquiescence, or failure to object at the earliest stage.
material_facts: The defendants initially admitted the court’s jurisdiction in their written statement and did not raise the issue when the original issues were framed.
The defendants later sought to amend their written statement to object to jurisdiction.
The suit concerned specific performance and possession of immovable property situated outside the court’s territorial jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The earlier admission and the delayed objection did not confer jurisdiction on the court or prevent the defendants from challenging it, because the defect concerned subject-matter jurisdiction; an order made by a court lacking jurisdiction is a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires objections to territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction to be raised at the earliest opportunity and, in the relevant circumstances, by or before settlement of issues. Subject-matter jurisdiction is distinct: where a statutory limitation deprives a court of jurisdiction over the subject matter, consent, waiver, or acquiescence cannot confer it, and an order made without jurisdiction is a nullity. The Court relied on Bahrein Petroleum Co. v. Pappu, Kiran Singh v. Chaman Paswan, and Setrucharlu v. Maharaja of Jeypore.

rule.if: civil_suit and subject_matter_jurisdiction_defect and (party_admitted_jurisdiction or objection_delayed)

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.subject_matter_jurisdiction_defect: A statutory limitation means the court lacks jurisdiction over the subject matter of the suit.
predicates.party_admitted_jurisdiction: A party admitted or consented to the court’s jurisdiction.
predicates.objection_delayed: A party raised the jurisdiction objection after an earlier procedural stage or after delay.

issues.definition: In a civil suit, an admission or delayed objection does not cure a defect that leaves the court without subject-matter jurisdiction.
